newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK customs seize cannabis, arrest German man.
newsitem.headline: HK customs seize cannabis, arrest German man.

text.p: Hong Kong customs officials seized a record 7.142 tonnes of cannabis on Saturday and arrested a German man alleged as the consignee of the illegal cargo, the government said.
The drugs, worth HK$327.5 million (US$42.4 million), were found in a container terminal and were believed destined for Europe, officials and government radio reported.
"We believe it (originated) from the Golden Triangle area," a senior customs official was quoted by government radio as saying.
"We believe the drugs were meant for European countries, I don't know if part of it would be consumed in Hong Kong," the official said.
The notorious Golden Triangle borders Thailand, Burma and Laos.
The official was also quoted as saying an international syndicate was believed to be behind the find.
"We have investigations on the syndicate behind which is international rather than based in Hong Kong," he said.
The name of the arrested German was not released.
